script: I did something during the war that saved thousands of lives, and I was never allowed to say a word about it. Not to my friends, not to my children, not even to my own wife. I signed a document swearing total silence for the rest of my life, no matter what happened after. Every single day, I solved problems that changed the outcome of the war. Every single night, I came home and said I filed paperwork in some forgotten office. My wife married a man she believed did nothing important at all, and I let her believe it for thirty years. In 1974, the government finally lifted the secrecy, and a book revealed everything. My wife read it before I ever said a word, and looked at me asking if it was true. This really happened, to the codebreakers of Britain's Bletchley Park, sworn to silence under the Official Secrets Act until 1974. I did something that saved thousands of lives, and couldn't tell my own wife for thirty years.
